chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Teschemacher's influences and talent
summary: Freeman says Tesch was influenced by Bix, Jimmy Noone and Omer Simeon, and might have become one of the greats had he lived.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: And so, to speak, you asked about Tesh. Tesh was very much, probably more influenced by Bix Beiderbecke than I was and very strongly influenced by Jimmy Noone, the great New Orleans clarinet player, who had a most unique style, and Tesh and I would just play together because we seemed to like each other's playing. We could play phrases together. There wasn't much music to read in Wingy's band, we had to know the charts.

And I think that if Tesh had lived, as you know, he was in an automobile accident and was instantly killed, if he had lived, he would have become one of the greats. Because he lived his music, he had a great talent for it and was also a great musician, could read anything in sight and could write and knew composition.
